content.short: dm3 is a messaging protocol focused on e2ee, scalability, decentralization, and interoperability.
content.description: dm3 provides a secure, intermediary-free method for exchanging messages. By standardizing how different messaging protocols, services, and dApps interact, it enables interoperability across diverse ecosystems. The protocol aligns messaging on a common set of specifications, making it easier for apps and services to connect, share data, and work together in a consistent and compatible manner. A common specification helps participants adopt and extend messaging capabilities in a consistent, predictable way.

resources.title: The Code Was Fine. That's the Problem.
resources.tldr: A long post-mortem on the KelpDAO exploit arguing the failure was in the trust layer, not the contracts. Makes the case that cross-chain bridges need cryptographic verification rather than multisig assurance.

resources.title: Pragmatic Adaptive Privacy
resources.tldr: Opens by admitting privacy was never a design goal of Bitcoin or Ethereum, which is why retrofitting it is so awkward. Long and unusually honest about the tradeoffs involved.

resources.title: Multi-Chain Apps and the Importance of Stateless Clients
resources.tldr: Every extra chain an app touches adds another RPC endpoint you have to trust. Explains how stateless clients verify data locally with proofs instead of taking a provider's word.
